Candidate reason labels for later review: ability to leave an unwanted relationship / `khả năng rời một quan hệ mình không muốn`; shared authority over common rules / `quyền cùng quyết định quy tắc chung`; protection when an individual loses a majority vote / `bảo vệ cá nhân khi họ thuộc phía thiểu số trong biểu quyết`; quickest useful help / `hỗ trợ có ích nhanh nhất`; confidence that the mechanism will work / `tin rằng cơ chế sẽ hoạt động`; other reason / `lý do khác`.

Do not enforce option/reason pairing. A respondent might choose A because ten households have urgent needs, because competing housing providers discipline managers, or because they distrust representation. B might express republican contestation, collective self-government, conservative stewardship of a shared place, or simple expectations of better rules. C might protect minorities, limit all officeholders, or minimize meeting burdens. None uniquely identifies a tradition.

Candidate reason labels: greatest unmet recipient need / `nhu cầu chưa được đáp ứng cao nhất của người được chăm sóc`; sustaining an unpaid caring relationship / `duy trì quan hệ chăm sóc không hưởng lương`; carers' claims to rest as persons in their own right / `quyền được nghỉ của người chăm sóc với tư cách một cá nhân`; equal shares of additional public support / `phần hỗ trợ công bổ sung bằng nhau`; reducing reliance on contested priority rankings / `giảm sự phụ thuộc vào cách xếp ưu tiên còn gây tranh luận`; responsibility for a voluntarily accepted role / `trách nhiệm đối với vai trò đã tự nguyện nhận`; other reason / `lý do khác`.

A could express recipient-centered capability, triage, or a narrow interpretation of the officer's duty. B could express care ethics, distributive concern for carers, or a consequentialist prediction that exhausted carers will stop providing care. C could express equal standing, skepticism about measurement, or an implementable rule. A respondent could favor B while holding a strongly family-centered worldview. A respondent could favor A while supporting extensive public care overall.

follow the agreed research purpose; test overlooked experiences; avoid assuming active residents represent everyone; produce evidence useful for a later challenge; preserve public trust in the association; use the strongest method for a specified question. A, B, and C each permit more than one motive. B is not evidence that a respondent rejects science; A is not evidence that they dismiss residents; C is not automatically the scientifically best compromise.

equal present membership; continuity of a local community; recognition of contribution; expectations attached to earlier public payments; encouraging future cooperation; avoiding penalties for unequal opportunities to contribute; administrative acceptability. B could express reliance interests rather than ethnic nationalism. C could express reciprocity rather than a belief that low contributors have less human worth. A could express equal civic standing, simple administration, or distrust of both classifications.

employment and household independence; duties to nonhuman life; preventing irreversible loss; caution under uncertain estimates; obligations to future people; a national leader's responsibility to livelihoods; confidence in enforceable conditions. A need not express indifference to nature: it may reflect a high value on local employment and a different view of acceptable risk. C may reflect nonhuman moral standing, anticipated future human benefits, or pessimism about contract enforcement. The last explanation should be recorded even though the case stipulates enforceability; it signals a possible credibility problem in the draft.

equal procedure now; an institution's responsibility for its own wrongs; current material disadvantage; acknowledging a group without assuming all members are alike; preventing renewed hierarchy; concern about institutional power to classify people; a view that course admission is or is not the appropriate remedy. A might accompany strong support for a different form of compensation. B might express reparative responsibility or a practical effort to rebuild institutional trust. C might express sufficientarian need, class analysis, or concern about who benefits within each community. Do not equate a selection with a complete view of caste, race, colonialism, merit, or equality.
